v1.feedback: The noctilucent concept genuinely drove the shader — below-horizon lighting, exposed-surface glow, ice-blue/silver palette with faint warm gold edge are all specific to the phenomenon, not generic reskins. Fixed camera at (28,18,32) will lose the form once growth fills past fog range; add a slow orbit or adaptive pull-back keyed to bounding radius. The warm-edge (0.06) and shimmer (0.04) multipliers are so low they'll be invisible on most monitors — bump to 0.10-0.12 so the noctilucent gold actually registers. Consider making the below-horizon light direction drift slowly over time to simulate the sun's position change that makes real noctilucent clouds pulse.

v2.feedback: Noctilucent vibe landed in the palette and lighting — ice-blue/silver base with below-horizon warm gold rim and mesospheric self-illumination on exposed cells is a coherent read. The parent's cellular morphogenesis is clearly preserved, not discarded. Two refinements: the shimmer uniform modulation (sin on viewPos) reads as a flat screen-space wash rather than localized ice-crystal scintillation — try keying it off surface curvature or exposure gradient so it clusters on ridges. Second, the warm gold edge at 0.12 strength is barely visible; push it to 0.25–0.35 so the twilight-lit-from-below effect actually registers as a second color temperature against the cool body, which is the defining visual of real noctilucent clouds.
